column3: “They are caught” is rendered as a wish, “Let them be caught.”
“He blesses” is rendered “curses”; NASB takes the Hebrew word in its opposite sense.
“His nose” is rendered “his countenance,” and NASB supplies “Him” after “seek”; “There is no God” is set as a quotation.
“His ways endure” is rendered “His ways prosper,” and NASB supplies “out of his sight”; “he breathes out at them” is rendered “he snorts at them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “his eyes lie hidden” is rendered “His eyes stealthily watch.”
The Hebrew is difficult (“an army of disheartened ones”); NASB renders the verse “He crouches, he bows down, And the unfortunate fall by his mighty ones.” The meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “You will not seek” is rendered “You will not require it.”
The Hebrew is difficult; “upon You he leaves” is rendered “commits himself to You,” and “You are a helper” as “You have been the helper.” The meaning is uncertain.
“And the evil one” is rendered “and the evildoer,” and “seek his wickedness, You will not find” as “until You find none.”
Close to the Hebrew; “You establish their heart” is rendered “You will strengthen their heart.”
“To terrify humankind from the earth” is rendered “man who is of the earth will no longer cause terror.”
